//: Example trace. Every step op pipeline/author.mjs understands is shown here, against
the local Express app in sample-app/ (target local-app), so it authors and records.
A trace is the observed walk of a .flow: Claude drives the real app in Chrome, does
each step, and writes down the element it touched, the selector that element answers
to, and HOW LONG each wait really took. author.mjs turns it into a .demo plus a
selector sidecar, sizing holds and narration from those measured times.
`name` is grammar-tour-trace, NOT grammar-tour: author.mjs writes scripts/<name>.demo
and would otherwise overwrite the hand-written scripts/grammar-tour.demo.
Keys starting with // are notes for people; author.mjs ignores them.
name: grammar-tour-trace
description: trace tour - every trace step op, recorded against the local Express app
//target: A target names the deployment. With no target, set "app": "http://localhost:3000" instead.
//startUrl: Where the take opens; becomes `start:`. Wins over the target's startUrl and may use {secret} placeholders, e.g. /chatbot/{agentId}/config.
resolvedBy: hand-authored example (selectors match sample-app/views/index.pug, not observed live)
provenance: scenarios/grammar-tour.trace.json - the example trace; there is no .flow behind it
//provenance: observedAt, resolvedBy and provenance are copied into the selector sidecar. Never claim 'observed live' for a hand-written trace.
intro: Trace tour | Every step a trace can hold
outro: Thanks for watching | Now write your own flow in input/
warnings:
Warnings are hazards the walk found that the script cannot express. Each one is copied
into the header of the generated .demo, so the next person to record reads it.
BEFORE EVERY TAKE: start the sample app (cd sample-app && npm start) so localhost:3000 answers.
